name: MathlibAnnex.BilipschitzOrientation.BiLipschitzOpenData
title: Inverse maps on open sets with global metric bounds

content.display_title: Inverse maps on open sets with global metric bounds
content.one_sentence_role: Records the maps, their inverse relations, and the quantitative bounds used in the orientation argument.
content.natural_language_statement: Fix $n\in\mathbb N_0$ and put $E=\mathbb R^n$ with the sup norm $\|\cdot\|_\infty$. The structure specifies open sets $S,T\subseteq E$ and maps $f,g:E\to E$. Their restrictions $f|_S:S\to T$ and $g|_T:T\to S$ are inverse bijections. Both maps have global Lipschitz bounds, and $f$ has a positive global lower bound.
content.definition_explanation:
Choose $S,T,f,g$ as above, constants $C_f,C_g\ge0$, and a real number $\ell>0$. Require the image and inverse relations
$$\begin{aligned}
f(S)&\subseteq T,&g(T)&\subseteq S,\\
g(f(x))&=x\quad(x\in S),&f(g(y))&=y\quad(y\in T),
\end{aligned}$$
and the three metric estimates
$$\ell\|x-x'\|_\infty\le\|f(x)-f(x')\|_\infty\le C_f\|x-x'\|_\infty\qquad(x,x'\in E),$$
$$\|g(y)-g(y')\|_\infty\le C_g\|y-y'\|_\infty\qquad(y,y'\in E).$$
Thus the upper and lower estimates concern all ambient points. They are additional global requirements; the inverse relations themselves are imposed only on the two open sets.
content.assumptions: The dimension $n$ may be zero. The sets $S$ and $T$ are open; neither connectedness, nonemptiness nor finite measure is required. The maps $f$ and $g$ are defined on all of $E$.
content.conclusion: The specified restrictions are inverse bijections between $S$ and $T$, with the displayed global bounds available for subsequent arguments. The definition does not require $f$ and $g$ to be inverse at every point outside those sets.
content.lean_realization_notes: These are chosen objects together with their stated properties, not an orientation or volume theorem. In particular, the global injectivity of $f$ is a consequence of the lower estimate, rather than an additional stored condition.
